hints.title: Max Length Subsequence Count Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the number of longest increasing subsequences requires tracking both the length of the longest chain ending at index i and the count of ways that maximum length was achieved. How can dual-property arrays update counts cleanly?

hints.title: Length Update Count Reset Invariant
hints.text: If extending from j creates a strictly longer chain at i, reset count[i] to count[j]. If it matches the existing maximum length at i, add count[j] to count[i].

hints.title: Dual Array Quadratic Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Initialize length array with 1s and count array with 1s. For each i, inspect all j < i: if nums[i] > nums[j], compare length[j] + 1 with length[i]. If strictly greater, update length[i] and set count[i] = count[j]. If equal, add count[j] to count[i]. Sum count[i] for all i where length[i] equals the global max length and return the sum.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (up to 2000)
complexity.notes: Nested loops compute length and count for every index.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all subsequences takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two 1D arrays of size N store length and count per index.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Resetting versus accumulating count when finding a strictly longer chain versus an equally long chain.
